title: Maternal and offspring fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes-associated genetic variants and cognitive function at age 8: a Mendelian randomization study in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children.
ehr_evidence: ALSPAC is a population-based prospective cohort study; data were collected from mothers and offspring from pregnancy onwards by questionnaire, abstraction from medical notes, record linkage and attendance at research clinics, and genetic variants were genotyped for this study.
summary: A Mendelian randomization study in the ALSPAC cohort examining whether maternal and offspring genetic variants associated with fasting glucose and T2D risk are causally related to child's IQ at age 8.
key_findings: The offspring FGGRS was strongly and positively associated with offspring fasting glucose (0.02 mmol/l per weighted allele, 95% CI 0.01, 0.03; p=7.1x10^-5) and HbA1c (0.02%, 95% CI 0.01, 0.02; p=1.6x10^-6), explaining 2-3% of trait variance.

No association was found between maternal or offspring FGGRS and child's IQ (maternal FGGRS mean difference 0.20, 95% CI -0.14, 0.53; p=0.26; offspring FGGRS mean difference -0.11, 95% CI -0.30, 0.07; p=0.22).

The maternal T2DGRS was positively associated with offspring IQ after adjustment for offspring T2DGRS and population stratification (mean difference 0.47 per weighted allele, 95% CI 0.12, 0.81; p=0.01).
Offspring of mothers with diabetes/glycosuria had lower IQ than children of non-diabetic mothers (mean difference -3.5, 95% CI -5.6, -1.5; p=0.001).
Fasting glucose was inversely associated with IQ but not significant (mean difference -1.94, 95% CI -4.71, 0.82; p=0.17); HbA1c was not associated with IQ.
captured_features: Maternal pre-pregnancy diabetes, gestational diabetes and glycosuria status
FGGRS and T2DGRS genetic risk scores
Confounders (maternal education, social class, age at delivery, parity, smoking, alcohol, breastfeeding, birthweight, gestational age, principal components)
study_design: Mendelian randomization study within a population-based prospective cohort (ALSPAC)
population: Mother-offspring pairs from the ALSPAC cohort (women around Bristol, England, delivered 1991-1992); cognitive testing of children at mean age 8 years 7 months
exposure_domain: Maternal and offspring glucose metabolism and type 2 diabetes genetic risk (fasting glucose and T2D-associated genetic variants/risk scores)
limitations: Lack of statistical power to reliably establish absence of association, with most individuals having fasting glucose and HbA1c within the normal range, limiting ability to detect effects at glucose extremes.
Some SNPs were out of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and individual variant associations with IQ disappeared after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing.
Maternal fasting glucose and HbA1c levels in pregnancy were not available, limiting validation of maternal exposure.
